title: Satay Tofu and Saucy Coconut Noodles
subtitle: with Wombok and Pickled Carrot
description: Hey speed freaks; sharpen a knife, tie your apron, brush off a chopping board, then GO! Our 25-minute recipes are ready before you know it, thanks to our hack-packed, fail-safe approach. Did we mention ‘yumness guaranteed’?

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil for the noodles. Cut the cabbage into 3cm chunks. Peel the carrot, then shred using a julienne peeler or coarsely grate with a box grater. Crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Put the Asian-style stock powder in a heatproof jug, add 125ml (½ cup) boiling water and stir to dissolve.
Pickle carrot: Combine 1 tbs white vinegar, 2 tsp soy sauce and 2 tsp sugar in a large bowl. Add the carrot and toss to combine. Set aside to pickle, tossing occasionally, until needed.

Cook noodles: Cook the noodles in the pan of boiling water for 2 mins or until tender. Drain, then rinse under hot water to prevent the noodles from sticking. Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the tofu for 2 mins each side or until golden and warmed through. Remove from the pan and cut into 1cm-thick strips.

Soften cabbage: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Cook the cabbage and garlic, stirring, for 2 mins or until softened. Stir in the coconut milk and stock and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 1 min.

Serve up: Add the noodles to the cabbage mixture and toss to combine. Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the noodle and cabbage mixture among bowls. Top with the tofu and drained pickled carrot and enjoy!

Did you know?: Chinese cabbage is a versatile veggie with a mild, sweet flavour. It can be shredded and eaten raw in coleslaw, used in stir-fries, for Korean kimchi or in soups and curries. It goes by many names, including wombok, wong bok, napa cabbage and celery cabbage.
